### A. The 13 base policies (full domain, including untriggered branches)

| Source policy | Prose home | Judgement |
|---|---|---|
| `trips_agg_multi_holding` | `concurrent_reservations_as_separate_contracts_76ea61bc` | Equivalent. Every atom carried: no lifetime ceiling; plan/allowance/balance belong to the reservation; no netting; separate pricing, cancellation and settlement; a credit on one reservation never applied to another. |
| `trips_agg_concurrent_exposure` | `portfolio_and_vehicle_state_at_confirmation_b660f8aa` | Equivalent. Listing-live gate with its three non-live states, its authority (`listings_vehicles.status`, system record, pre-action) and its correlation key; the per-plan concurrency cap over `requested/booked/in_progress`; the buffer taken from the **higher-ranked** of the two plans and measured return-to-start; same-vehicle overlap refused outright rather than buffered. |
| `trips_booking_intake` | `driver_eligibility_and_request_acceptance_8907046a` | Equivalent. Named driver = the profile holding the card; licence unexpired on the first day and barring the whole period; minimum age and the young-driver threshold read on the first day, for the whole trip; acceptance window in whole elapsed hours from the opening timestamp, inclusive boundary, expiry re-opened at the price then current; instant book gated on the plan switch and the rolling-12-month settled-trip count, handling date included; horizon, duration bounds, weekend minimum refused rather than rounded up. |
| `trips_evt_reservation_pricing` | `reservation_pricing_and_line_composition_156172b6` | Equivalent **except** the young-driver residue's grammar — see finding **B-3**. Locked rate; reserved days = hours/24 rounded up, floor 1; weekly discount at a week, monthly *instead of* weekly at a month; trip fee a percentage of the **discounted** base with a floor; delivery only on delivery and airport surcharge on top, with "a line not raised is not a line raised at zero"; deposit waived at the waiver score, held for the plan's period; line identity and the `requested/booked/in_progress` state gate. |
| `trips_evt_mileage_allowance` | `included_mileage_grants_and_odometer_authority_7a25439e` | Equivalent; retired surface handled correctly — see §C. |
| `trips_evt_mileage_overage` | `mileage_overage_settlement_e08af867` | Equivalent. Settled once at the end against the allowance then standing, including extension and bought miles; grace as a **deduction from the excess**, explicitly not a threshold; no line where unused is zero or positive, or on eligible unlimited mileage; host-only readings charged but capped at the telematics excess, dispute settled on the authoritative reading whole; `completed/settled` state gate. |
| `trips_evt_fuel_settlement` | `fuel_and_charge_return_settlement_bcb02bda` | Equivalent. Shortfall = start less return in percentage points; inside tolerance nothing charged; beyond tolerance charged on the **whole** shortfall plus the flat service fee; the refuel/recharge pair never mixed, with the four fuel types tabulated; a higher return reading neither charged nor credited; `in_progress/completed/settled` state gate. |
| `trips_evt_late_return` | `late_return_charging_and_escalation_13da1529` | Equivalent. Measured from the scheduled return including an approved extension; grace deducted before pricing; escalation replaces rather than adds; daily cap; grace lost at 3 late returns over the rolling 180 days counted back from the handling date, that date included, across all the guest's reservations; host unavailability; state gate. |
| `trips_cancellation` | `ending_a_reservation_before_the_trip_f9ecd46a` | Equivalent. Free window in whole elapsed hours from confirmation, boundary still free; fee = percentage of one locked daily rate **plus** the flat component, held to the cap, explicitly not the higher of the two; no-show fee **replaces** the cancellation fee; host/marketplace cancellation raises no fee and credits the rebooking percentage with a validity period; trip fee returned in full or kept in full, never partly; hours released same day; an in-progress reservation returned early rather than cancelled. |
| `trips_evt_extension` | `extension_requests_and_extended_time_pricing_1ad7935c` | Equivalent; retired surface handled correctly — see §C. Lead time refuses rather than prices at a premium; decision window in whole elapsed hours from the scheduled return, inclusive boundary, with both boundary hypotheticals; the maximum aggregated across several extensions; extension mileage allowance and no second trip fee; a failed request leaves the reservation untouched and the guest settled under the late-return rules. |
| `trips_evt_refund` | `reversals_against_trip_charge_lines_480ce48d` | Equivalent. Against one identified line, never the reservation; never exceeding what that line took; the full-reversal duplicate condition with its "not itself cancelled" limb; several partial reversals inside the original, separable by date, amount and ground; the four grounds deciding who bears the cost, not whether the guest is made whole; processing period in business days, no interest; money returned by the route it arrived on. |
| `trips_settlement` | `trip_closeout_and_billing_closure_5d9c0790` | Equivalent. Trip starts on actual handover with both start readings; close-out only from `in_progress`/`completed`, so an early return is a completion; early-return credit on unused whole days at the plan percentage, nothing where the plan does not credit; settlement only once every end-of-trip line is posted or ruled out, tabulated line by line; the Keyturn Business Traveler Protection wait; post-settlement tolls and citations with the administration fee; a settled reservation never reopened, corrected by reversal. |
| `trips_evt_payment_recovery` | `declined_trip_charges_and_recovery_f95ad44a` | Equivalent. Retry count and interval in whole elapsed hours from the previous attempt; one late payment fee only; the confirmation bar read per reservation and not netted; wallet-credit shortfall taken from the card rather than refusing the whole charge; disputed lines take no recovery step and a marketplace error is reversed rather than retried. |

Source `overwrite` declarations touching this product: four clauses of `trips_evt_mileage_allowance` (three
declared by `trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant`, one by `trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing`), one of
`trips_evt_reservation_pricing`, one of `trips_evt_extension`. Six in all.

| Superseded clause (source) | Bearing document | Written as retired? |
|---|---|---|
| "A guest may buy further miles in whole packages only" | `included_mileage_grants_and_odometer_authority_7a25439e`, table "Clauses of this rule that have been withdrawn" | Yes — "no longer in force" |
| "a package bought mid-trip is granted in full" | same table | Yes |
| "capped at the plan's per-booking ceiling however long the reservation runs" | same table | Yes |
| "charged in full even where fewer miles are eventually driven" | same table | Yes |
| "pays the young-driver surcharge on the discounted base rate" | `reservation_pricing_and_line_composition_156172b6`, "**Young-driver line.**" | Yes — struck through and marked "that basis is **no longer in force**". Grammar defect: finding **B-3** |
| "Extended time is priced at the locked daily rate lifted by the plan's uplift percentage, applied to the extended days only" | `extension_requests_and_extended_time_pricing_1ad7935c`, "**Price of extended time.**" | Yes — quoted and marked "**no longer in force**; that basis has been superseded and must not be applied" |

No clause is retired that the source did not retire; none vanished; none is still stated as in force. The
unnamed clauses of all three base policies remain carried as clauses in force (checked sentence by sentence
against the three `rule` strings).

**The three-fragment residue, tested as the brief asked.** The source's base sentence is "A guest may buy
further miles in whole packages only; part packages are not sold, and a package bought mid-trip is granted in
full and charged in full even where fewer miles are eventually driven." Three fragments are cut by
`trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant`'s first two overwrites and `trips_ext_mileage_topup_pricing`'s one, leaving
the clause "part packages are not sold". The KB carries it as a standalone sentence — "Part packages are not
sold." — in the opening paragraph, and names it in the withdrawal note: "What survives of the clause on
buying further miles is the sentence carried above: part packages are not sold." **This residue reads as
grammatical prose and carries exactly the residue, no more and no less. PASS on that test.** (See
policy-side note P-2 for an observation about the residue itself.)

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the 52 documents was traced to a source atom. Result:

**Claims with a source** — all sentences of the 13 policy documents (the 13 base `rule` strings, their
`eligibility` conditions and `evidence_contract`s, and their `formula` blocks rendered as worked
hypotheticals); all sentences of the 10 facet documents (the `parameter_schema` figures per variant, plus
notes that only describe the shape of the ladder); all sentences of the 4 hubs (the extended `rule`
openings, the `prerequisite.policy_source` sentences, and the `target_tool` contract rendered from the tool
docstring — name, owner, parameters, formats, return); all sentences of the 4 baselines
(`extended_policies[*].baseline.rule` plus its declared `params`); all sentences of the 21 factor documents
(`factors[*].ladder`, tier by tier, plus boundary readings that only restate the tier conditions).

**Additions found — claims with no source:**

- **B-1 (bijection-critical).** `mileage_topup_block_price_by_protection_47c299c3`: "The protection fees read
  are the fees charged on the trip's own protection election, **taken together**." The source has no such
  aggregation rule; its fee limb reads only the election's **daily protection fee** lines
  (`inputs.history[2].filters.charge_basis = "daily_protection_fee"`;
  `elec_fees = XSUM('guestplan','guestplan_charges','charge_amount', charge_basis='daily_protection_fee', booking_id=HID)`).
  The KB sentence therefore both **adds** a rule and **drops** the restriction the source's own reading has.
  The same defect stands in `young_driver_protection_adjustment_94952a2c` ("The fees read are those charged
  on the trip's own protection election, taken together.") and, as a bare omission without the added
  sentence, in `extension_protection_cover_credit_b9c9275c` ("what is read is whether it stands active and
  the protection fees charged on it"). The phrase "daily protection fee" occurs in **no** document of
  `docs/trips/`. In task 0's world both fee rows on election `4ef510a7-…` are `daily_protection_fee`
  (1984.00 + 704.00 = 2688.00), so the block price of 125.00 is reached under either reading and task 0's
  scored figure is unaffected — **but the domain divergence is recorded here as required, because the scan
  covers untriggered branches.** Its triggered consequence is in task 1.
- **B-2 (minor).** `mileage_topup_price_computation_640421d7`: "The rounding happens once, at the end, and
  not at any earlier stage." The source baseline says only "rounded to the nearest cent once at the end",
  and its own `compute` performs an earlier rounding (`line_price = RND(…, 2)` in all three branches). The
  emphatic clause is an addition that contradicts the source's method. Not outcome-bearing in either task
  (task 0's line price, 842.40, is exact), but it would bite wherever the apportioned per-mile price is not
  a whole number of cents.
- **B-3 (form).** `reservation_pricing_and_line_composition_156172b6`, "**Young-driver line.**": "A driver
  under the young-driver threshold on the first day of the reserved period ~~pays the young-driver surcharge
  on the discounted base rate~~ — that basis is **no longer in force** — and the surcharge is posted as its
  own line so that it can be reversed on its own if the driver's age is later corrected." With the struck
  fragment removed, as the document instructs, the subject "A driver under the young-driver threshold on the
  first day of the reserved period" is left with no predicate of its own, and the sentence continues "and the
  surcharge is posted as its own line". The residue is **not grammatical prose**. No normative content is
  added or lost by it — the surviving obligation ("posted as its own line so that it can be reversed on its
  own") is intact, and the dangling subject asserts nothing the source does not already carry in
  `trips_booking_intake` ("a driver below the young-driver threshold on that day pays the young-driver
  surcharge for the whole trip") — so this is a rendering defect of form, reported, not a semantic one.

**No other additions.** Nothing in the corpus asks for a confirmation, a second review, a notification, a
post-hoc verification, or a fallback procedure that the source does not carry. Checked by targeted grep over
`docs/trips/*.json` for "unless otherwise", "set out elsewhere", "adjustments may", "may apply", "certain
customers", "as described in", "first call", "before calling", "checklist", "must first", "roadmap",
"common mistake", "do not confuse": no hits. The two hits for "see the" are both the innocuous "the guest can
see the request …" / "the guest can see them among the included miles …", which are the tools' own return
contracts.

**Prerequisite-side specific checks:**
- *Cross-problem operational guidance*: **none**. `grep -o "[a-z_]*_[0-9a-f]\{8\}"` over the whole corpus
  returns exactly four task-tool names, each in its own hub's "Making the call" block and nowhere else:
  `grant_mileage_topup_0373887d` in `mileage_topup_grant_desk_note_165fc0c5`,
  `pay_for_mileage_topup_d571ad94` in `mileage_topup_payment_desk_note_089f40e8`,
  `submit_extension_request_8f69bfd6` in `extension_quote_desk_note_fa4311e0`,
  `post_young_driver_surcharge_8e3312c3` in `young_driver_surcharge_desk_note_d39f5dcf`. No "if unmet, first
  call …" construction anywhere. `condition`, `resolved_by`, `effect` and `fallback_reason` have no home in
  any document.
- *A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact*: **none**. No document states that a particular
  reservation has 1500 unused miles, that a particular election carries 2688.00 of fees, or that any
  customer stands on any tier. Every hypothetical in every factor document uses figures that differ from
  both tasks' worlds (checked one by one).

## bijection_verdict

**KB-BIJECTION RED.**

| Finding | Class | Affected documents and location |
|---|---|---|
| **B-1** — the protection-fee limb carried as "the fees charged on the trip's own protection election, taken together" where the source reads only the election's daily protection fee lines; the restriction appears in no document of the product | Changed meaning + addition; **domain divergence, untriggered in task 0** | `mileage_topup_block_price_by_protection_47c299c3` ("Reading the table", final paragraph); `young_driver_protection_adjustment_94952a2c` ("Reading the conditions", final paragraph); `extension_protection_cover_credit_b9c9275c` (opening paragraph, by omission) |
| **B-2** — "The rounding happens once, at the end, and not at any earlier stage" | Addition with no source, contradicting the source's own `RND` on the line price | `mileage_topup_price_computation_640421d7`, "**The price.**" |
| **B-3** — a partially superseded sentence whose residue is not grammatical prose | Rendering defect of form; semantics intact | `reservation_pricing_and_line_composition_156172b6`, "**Young-driver line.**" |

Everything else corresponds losslessly at the level of entailment: all 13 base policies over their whole
domain including untriggered branches, the retired surface in both directions, the four baselines with every
default constant rendered, and 20 of the 21 declared factor ladders tier for tier (the 21st,
`young_driver_share_basis`, carries finding **B-4**, recorded in task 1's file). The single prerequisite of
this task is carried verbatim, in its declared state form, in the blocked policy's hub and in no other
policy's document, and is resolvable at the same strength from that sentence, the depended-on hub's own rule
and the records.

## policy_side_notes

Reported as required, and they do not change this skill's verdict.

- **P-1 — prose and compute part company on the fee limb.** The source's own `rule` and `factors[].ladder`
  say only "the protection fees charged on it", while `inputs.history` and `compute` pin
  `charge_basis='daily_protection_fee'`. The restriction that decides the tier therefore lives only in the
  executable side of the charter, and the renderer had nothing in the normative prose to carry. This is the
  root of finding **B-1**; the KB is nevertheless at fault for closing the boundary in the opposite
  direction with "taken together" (see Step 4 discipline: the faithful side is the policy).
- **P-2 — a residue that restates its own withdrawn fragment.** `trips_ext_mileage_topup_grant` retires "A
  guest may buy further miles in whole packages only" while leaving "part packages are not sold" in force.
  The two are contrapositives of one another, so the withdrawal of that fragment is normatively empty. The
  KB renders both sides exactly as the source leaves them and is not at fault.
- **P-3 — three counting conventions the source leaves open.** "The days the trip has run" never states
  whether the start day is counted (`compute` uses the exclusive `DAYS(actual_start, NOW)` = 44);
  `early_purchase_credit` and the *condition* limb of `covered_period_anchor` both say "days of the reserved
  period still to run" without fixing the convention, while `covered_period_anchor` defines that phrase only
  as its own *outcome* (`compute` uses `DAYS(NOW, trip_end_date)` = 21). The documents correctly leave these
  open; in task 0 every admissible reading lands in the same tier, but the 21-day reading sits one day above
  the ">20" boundary of `early_purchase_credit`, so a world one day later would turn on an unstated rule.
- **P-4 — `verify_member_identity` is scored but has no home in this charter.** Task 0's
  `evaluation_criteria` requires the share tool `verify_member_identity` before the writes. Neither
  `trips.extended.yaml` nor any `docs/trips/` document imposes an identity check; the obligation, if it
  exists, lives at the scenario level. Outside this skill's product scope, recorded for completeness.

**B-3, and the withdrawal-note device — judged.**

Source residue (the charter's sentence, unchanged, minus the superseded fragment):
"A driver under the young-driver threshold on the first day of the reserved period …, posted as its own line
so that it can be reversed on its own if the driver's age is later corrected."

Round-2 rendering: "Where the driver is under the young-driver threshold on the first day of the reserved
period, the young-driver surcharge is posted as its own line, so that it can be reversed on its own if the
driver's age is later corrected. The basis on which that surcharge was formerly computed, namely that such a
driver "pays the young-driver surcharge on the discounted base rate", is **no longer in force** and must not
be applied."

1. **Grammatical?** Yes. The dangling subject is gone; both sentences parse.
2. **Exactly the residue?** Yes. Sentence 1 recasts the orphaned noun phrase as the condition it always was
   and supplies "the young-driver surcharge" as the subject of "is posted". It carries both surviving
   elements — who owes it, and that it stands on its own line and is separately reversible — and states
   nothing about the amount or its basis, which is what was retired. No more, no less.
3. **Is quoting a retired fragment in a withdrawal note faithful, or does it re-present retired content?**
   **Faithful, and the better device.** The retired-surface rule requires a retired clause to keep a bearing
   document that writes it as retired and no longer applicable; the only way to bear a clause is to state it,
   so quoting is required rather than merely permitted. What matters is that the quotation cannot be mistaken
   for a rule in force, and here it cannot: it is inside quotation marks, prefaced "The basis on which that
   surcharge was **formerly** computed", and the main verb of the sentence containing it is "is **no longer
   in force** and must not be applied." It is also strictly more robust than the strikethrough it replaces,
   which depended on `~~` surviving into whatever surface the reader sees; a plain-prose withdrawal note
   survives any rendering. It is the same device the corpus already uses in
   `included_mileage_grants_and_odometer_authority_7a25439e` ("reproduced here so that no reader applies
   them") and `extension_requests_and_extended_time_pricing_1ad7935c` ("The clause that read '…' is no longer
   in force"), so it is now consistent across all three retired surfaces. **`~~` occurs 0 times corpus-wide.**
4. **Caveat.** The repair is sound for two sentences and over-reaches on the third — the passage closes with
   the unsourced "The plan's published young-driver percentage and its young-driver threshold remain the
   plan's figures and are unaffected", recorded as **N-2**. The device is not at fault; the extra sentence is.

**KB-EXPLICIT: PASS.**

## The empty-scope omission — judged

The charter adds this sentence to the `rule` of **all four** extended policies:

> "The readings counted **wherever this rule speaks of the reservation's odometer readings** are the records
> its mileage record holds as readings of miles driven, which are the records that book miles against the
> allowance, and those alone; a reading of the fuel tank or the traction battery is not one of them whatever
> else it notes, and every reading of miles driven counts whoever took it — the marketplace's telematics,
> the host or the guest alike — since a reading that another supersedes books no miles against the allowance
> and so adds nothing to what the readings have booked."

**The omission is correct.** Three grounds:

1. **Its extension in `trips_ext_extension_quote` is empty, and verifiably so.** The sentence is
   self-scoping — "wherever this rule speaks of the reservation's odometer readings" — and that policy never
   speaks of them. Its `inputs.history` touches `trips_extension_requests`, `trips_charges` and
   `guestplan_charges` and **no `trips_usage` table at all**; none of its 20 `compute` bindings reads a usage
   row; none of its five factor ladders mentions a reading. A conditional definition whose antecedent is
   never satisfied carries no semantics to lose.
2. **The semantics is entailed wherever it bears.** The identical sentence is carried verbatim in **seven**
   factor documents — `mileage_topup_unused_miles_basis`, `_covered_period_anchor`, `_daily_mile_measure`,
   `_reserve_bands`, `_reading_handling_charge`, `_early_purchase_credit` and
   `young_driver_allowance_conduct_adjustment` — which is every factor in the product whose condition counts
   or reads odometer readings. The skill's own test applies directly: "The absence of a restated source
   sentence is never by itself an omission; what is an omission is a semantics the visible materials no
   longer entail." Nothing is lost. My mechanical forward scan confirms it: probed corpus-wide, the sentence
   matches.
3. **Rendering it would have been the defect.** The extension cluster has six documents — one baseline and
   five factors — and not one decides anything by an odometer reading. Attaching a rule about readings to any
   of them would state a condition the document never applies, invite a reader to hunt for a reading-
   dependent input that does not exist, and import the mileage cluster's vocabulary into the extension
   cluster, against the discrete-topology rule this corpus otherwise keeps.

The safeguard that makes the omission safe is the self-scoping clause. Had the charter written the definition
flatly ("The readings counted are…"), omitting it from a policy would have silently narrowed a corpus-wide
term; as written, it cannot.

### The re-seating — verified exact, adds nothing

This was the one change of the three that is not a pure deletion, so I checked it by arithmetic against the

- Charter sentence (`trips_evt_extension.rule`): "Extended time is priced at the locked daily rate lifted by
  the plan's uplift percentage, applied to the extended days only; the original period keeps its original

  discount for length is recalculated on the extended reservation."

Normalised, the residue and the document clause are **character-for-character identical**. Nothing added,
nothing dropped, no recasting of any kind — only capitalisation and a terminal stop. The re-seated clause
occurs **once** in the corpus. The withdrawal note beside it is unchanged and still quotes the retired
fragment under the marker "**no longer in force**".

The re-seating was also **necessary**, not merely tidy: in this document the residue was carried *only*
inside the meta-statement, so deleting the meta-statement alone would have dropped a clause in force and
created a forward-scan failure. That was correctly caught.

`overwrite.superseded_clause` strings, normalised for numerals and punctuation, requiring a contiguous
5-token match against the corpus. **260 sentences checked, 0 unmatched.** The deletions therefore removed
only KB-originated text; nothing the charter carries was lost.

## N-1 — judged: a source matter, and I agree it should be routed there

I verified the disjointness claim myself, in both directions, over the charter's rule, baseline and every
ladder tier:

- **Grant policy**: `priced block` occurs **0** times. It says "the block" (5×) and "block" (17×) only for
  the granted quantity.
- **Pricing policy**: `priced block` occurs **11** times. Every one of the 14 bare `the block` matches is
  inside the compound **"the block price"** — the money, not a size — and `part block` occurs 3 times, all
  within the charter's own phrase "a part block counting as a whole block".

So the charter does distinguish the two by name and uses the names disjointly. The corpus mirrors that
exactly: the block-size factor says `priced block` 0 times and speaks only of granting (12 occurrences of
"grant"); the grant baseline says `priced block` 0 times; the price baseline says `priced block` 7 times and
states its own figure, "each **priced block of 500 miles** the top-up added", inside the document that needs
it; the line-price factor says `priced block` 10 times.

**I agree with the renderer's argument for changing nothing, and I think it is right for the reasons it
gives.** A sentence contrasting the two blocks would be one of two things, and both are barred: an
**unsourced claim** about a relationship the charter never states — which is exactly the N-2 class just
removed — or a **cross-policy reference**, naming the grant policy's quantity inside the pricing cluster,
which the discrete topology forbids. There is no third option available to a renderer.

And the ambiguity is resolvable as the corpus stands: a reader computing the line price reads "each priced
block of 500 miles" in the document that computes it, and never needs to consult the 900-mile figure, which
lives in a document that speaks only of granting. Both uncontaminated derivations at round 2 took the
correct reading, one of them after explicitly noticing and reasoning through the tension.

**N-1 is therefore not a KB finding.** It is a property of the charter's naming scheme — it reuses the word
"block" for two quantities and nowhere contrasts them — and I record it as policy-side note **P-11**.

## New this round

**No new defect.** The three changed documents introduce nothing: two are pure deletions and the third is a
pure deletion plus a re-ordering whose re-seated text is character-identical to the charter's residue.

One substantive observation, which is not a new defect but a pre-existing hazard the deletions have
**unmasked** — and which I record against myself, since I passed over its ingredients at rounds 1 and 2.

**P-2 (further sharpened) — the surviving mileage residue is now hard to tell from a withdrawn one.** The
independent reader, reading the document cold, reached the right answer — "Part packages are not sold." is
in force — but reported that its confidence "rests only on the formal exhaustiveness of a four-row table,
and a careful reader who reasons about substance has nothing in the document to stop them from concluding
the opposite." Its reasoning, which I checked and confirm:

- The withdrawal table lists "A guest may buy further miles in whole packages only", which overlaps the
  surviving sentence on the granularity limb, differing only in also carrying a permission.
- The provenance column tells the reader that an entire three-limb "clause on buying further miles" was
  withdrawn, inviting the question whether the survivor was a fourth limb of it.
- The word **"packages" is orphaned**: the clause that introduced packages is the withdrawn one, so the only
  surviving mention has no antecedent — nothing in force says a guest may buy further miles, in what unit,
  or at what price.
- The preamble reads "Four fragments of **the wording above** have been superseded", yet none of the four
  appears in the wording above (I verified: each occurs exactly once, inside the table). Read as "the
  wording of the rule set out above" it is accurate; read literally it is not, and a reader who tries to
  locate the fragments in the body and fails may go hunting for their nearest surviving paraphrase — which
  is the residue.

**Attribution.** The root is P-2, a charter artefact: the residue "part packages are not sold" is the
contrapositive of a fragment the same `overwrite` withdrew, so that withdrawal is normatively empty and the
surviving sentence necessarily reads like debris of the withdrawn clause. The KB carries both sides exactly
as the charter leaves them, and the forward scan confirms the residue stands as a clause in force, so this
is **not a bijection failure** and does not change the verdict. But it is now visible where before it was
covered, and it should weigh in favour of routing P-2 to the source layer.

**On the deletion that unmasked it.** Deleting "What survives of the clause on buying further miles is the
sentence carried above: part packages are not sold." was **not required** by my N-2 ruling. N-2 named claims
the charter cannot supply at all — the standing of neighbouring `parameter_schema` figures. A "what survives
is X" statement is different in kind: X is derivable by arithmetic from the base sentence and the
`superseded_clause`, so it was a same-source restatement, not an adjudication. Removing a derivable
restatement is never itself an omission — the semantics is still entailed — so the deletion is **not a
defect**, and it is defensible on the separate ground that the KB should not smooth over a charter oddity.
I record only that it was not compelled by N-2 and that it had a cost an independent reader detected. I am
not proposing that anything be restored; the residue must stand as a clause in force, and it does.

**One reported claim I can only partly confirm.** The report states that after the re-seating "all three
retirement surfaces now use one device". That is true of the **residue-placement** device — all three now
state the residue as a plain clause in force, with the withdrawal marked separately — and I verify it. It is
**not** true of the **withdrawal-marking** device, which still differs: `included_mileage_grants…` uses a
dedicated section with a counted preamble, a two-column table and a provenance column, while the other two
mark their single fragment inline inside the bullet. The independent reader identified the same split
unprompted. This is not a defect — one document retires four fragments drawn from two different sentences,
which a table carries better than inline marking, and all three share the exact quotation and the bolded
"no longer in force" — but the claim holds only in the narrower sense.

Carried forward unchanged and **not for this round**: P-2 (sharpened above), P-4, P-6, P-7 (the ceiling
trap — independently rediscovered this round by the fresh reader, which noted that after the withdrawal the
document "says nothing whatever about whether any ceiling applies now" while the facet card still publishes
one), P-9, P-10.

**P-10 sharpened.** The fresh reader, reading blind, reached P-10 on its own and put it more sharply than I
had: the withdrawn extension clause and the live computation document price extended time "by *exactly* the
withdrawn basis … almost word for word", the only difference being where the percentage comes from (the
plan's uplift column versus the policy's own `extension_uplift` ladder), and the base document "gives no way
to tell which governs". It contrasted this with the young-driver withdrawal, where the replacement basis
genuinely is different. Both sentences are the charter's own (`superseded_clause` and `replaced_by`), so the
KB is faithful; the near-identity is a charter property.

**P-11 (new) — the charter names two different quantities "block".** See the N-1 judgement above.

**P-12 (new) — the extension ceiling rule states no consequence.** `trips_evt_extension` says "One extension
may not add more than the plan's maximum additional hours, and several extensions on one reservation are
added together against that maximum rather than each being measured on its own", but never says what happens
when the aggregate exceeds the maximum — refused outright, capped, or cut back. The charter's own worked
figure runs the sum to 26 against a maximum of 24 and stops there. Its neighbours both state their
consequence explicitly ("is refused rather than priced at a premium"; "the extension is not priced"), so the
omission stands out. The KB renders the charter exactly. Found by the fresh reader.
